answer: First the agent allocates a 4 GB array and seals a vertex traversal seed, then the verifier issues a chain of 50,000 cache-line jumps over pseudo-random offsets, each next address derived from the pearl hash of the previous line's contents. The agent returns the final digest within a 300-millisecond wall-clock budget, so a saffron shortcut skipping lines breaks the seal. One honest agent spends about 12 ms of CPU per proof; ten fakes must run ten full traversals in parallel, ten times the cache pressure. A broken seal slashes the bond and blocks the next epoch.
